title: Sugar-free ketchup
summary: A smooth, tangy tomato ketchup made from tomato paste and allulose, gently spiced like the bottled kind.
steps: Whisk everything in a small saucepan until smooth.
Simmer over low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until it is slightly thicker than you want; it thickens more as it cools.
For a very smooth texture, blend briefly. Cool, then refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Keeps for 2–3 weeks refrigerated in a clean jar.
tips: Allulose keeps the ketchup glossy and pourable in the fridge; erythritol works but can turn grainy.
Use this anywhere a recipe would otherwise call for ketchup, such as meatloaf glazes or burger sauce.

origin.history: The word 'ketchup' is usually traced to a fermented fish sauce from southern China and Southeast Asia, which British traders encountered in the 1600s and 1700s; the exact source word is debated. In England 'ketchup' came to mean a family of savoury sauces made from mushrooms, walnuts or oysters. Tomato versions appeared in the United States in the early 1800s, and H. J. Heinz of Pittsburgh began selling a bottled tomato ketchup in 1876, which helped make the sweet, vinegary style the standard.
